name: binMeans
title: Fast mean calculations in non-overlapping bins

origin.description: Computes the sample means in non-overlapping bins.
origin.usage:
binMeans(y, x, idxs = NULL, bx, na.rm = TRUE, count = TRUE,
  right = FALSE, ...)

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: A numeric or logical vector of K values to calculate means on.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A numeric vector of K positions for to be binned.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: A vector indicating the subset of elements to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: bx
arguments.text: A numeric vector of B + 1 ordered positions specifying the B > 0 bins [bx[1], bx[2]), [bx[2], bx[3]), ..., [bx[B], bx[B + 1]).

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values in y are dropped before calculating the mean, otherwise not.

arguments.name: count
arguments.text: If TRUE, the number of data points in each bin is returned as attribute count, an integer vector of length B.

arguments.name: right
arguments.text: If TRUE, the bins are right-closed (left open), otherwise left-closed (right open).

origin.details: binMeans(x, bx, right = TRUE) gives equivalent results as rev(binMeans(-x, bx = sort(-bx), right = FALSE)), but is faster. Data points where either of y and x is missing are dropped, and therefore are also not counted. Non-finite values in y are not allowed and give an error. Missing values in bx are not allowed and give an error.
origin.value: A numeric vector of length B.
origin.example:
x <- 1:200
mu <- double(length(x))
mu[1:50] <- 5
mu[101:150] <- -5
y <- mu + rnorm(length(x))

bx <- c(0, 50, 100, 150, 200) + 0.5
y_s <- binMeans(y, x = x, bx = bx)

plot(x, y)
for (kk in seq_along(y_s)) {
  lines(bx[c(kk, kk + 1)], y_s[c(kk, kk)], col = "blue", lwd = 2)
}

translation.description: Computes the sample means in non-overlapping bins.
translation.usage: binMeans(y, x, bx, idxs=None, na_rm=True, count=True, right=True)

arguments.name: y
arguments.text: A one-dimensional numeric or logical vector of K values to average. Logical values are 1 and 0. Infinite values are an error when y is floating point.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A one-dimensional numeric vector of K positions to be binned. Missing positions are dropped, together with the paired y value.

arguments.name: bx
arguments.text: A numeric vector of B + 1 ordered break points. The bins are [bx[j], bx[j + 1]) when right is false.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: A 1-based subscript applied to both y and x, with the same rules as R's x[idxs]. None keeps every element.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If True, missing values in y are dropped before the mean is calculated. This is na.rm in R. Missing x is always dropped.

arguments.name: count
arguments.text: If True, the number of data points in each bin is attached as the integer count attribute.

arguments.name: right
arguments.text: If True, the bins are right-closed and left-open, (bx[j], bx[j + 1]]. If False, they are left-closed and right-open. The default is True.

translation.details: Means and counts come from the binmeans crate, a port of matrixStats src/binMeans.c. Pairs are ordered by x before the bins are filled. A position that lands on a break belongs to the closed side of that break. An empty bin has a NaN mean and a zero count. Missing bx is an error.
translation.value: A one-dimensional float array of length B. When count is true, the result is a BinMeansResult whose count attribute is an int32 array of length B.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matrixstats.binmeans import binMeans

x = np.arange(1, 201)
mu = np.zeros(x.size)
mu[:50] = 5
mu[100:150] = -5
y = mu + np.random.default_rng(1).normal(size=x.size)
bx = np.array([0, 50, 100, 150, 200]) + 0.5
y_s = binMeans(y, x, bx)

plt.plot(x, y)
for kk, mean in enumerate(y_s):
    plt.plot(bx[kk:kk + 2], [mean, mean], color="blue", linewidth=2)
